newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Kinkel hails NATO-Russia deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kinkel hails NATO-Russia deal.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel on Wednesday hailed an agreement between NATO Secretary General Javier Solana and Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov making way for a NATO-Russia security deal on May 27.

Solana and Primakov agreed the text of the deal in Moscow on Wednesday intended to forge a peaceful new relationship after years of mistrust and sweep away Moscow's concerns over the expansion of the Western defence alliance.

Kinkel, who has played a significant role in diplomatic efforts to make NATO's plans to expand into eastern Europe more palatable to Russia, said he hoped the "preliminary" agreement would lead to closer cooperation between NATO and Moscow.

"This preliminary agreement reached during the negotiations on a NATO-Russia document is good news. Solana's persistent negotiations as well as my countless talks with Primakov have paid off," Kinkel said in a statement.

"Russia must be fully involved in Europe's new security architecture. We do not want any (security) troughs in Europe. I hope that the result of these talks will help to open the door to closer security cooperation with Russia," he said.
The text was agreed after months of tough negotiations between the two former Cold War foes and is likely to be signed in Paris on May 27.
